entity.summary: Global centralized cryptocurrency exchange launched under the BitMax name in July 2018 and later rebranded as AscendEX. The exchange ceased operations effective July 1, 2026 after citing its lack of MiCA authorization and broader regulatory, financial, and operational considerations; limited account access remains for wind-down and offboarding purposes.
entity.notes: Official company material establishes the July 2018 BitMax launch and later AscendEX identity. AscendEX stated that operations ceased effective 2026-07-01. New accounts, deposits, trading, swaps, staking, lending, referrals, and promotional services are no longer available. From 2026-07-06, automated withdrawals were paused and all withdrawal requests became subject to manual review, with no assurance on timing or amounts. HEI uses death_reason unknown because the official notice cites MiCA authorization, broader regulatory, financial, and operational considerations, and a failed strategic transaction without establishing a single confirmed terminal cause or a formal insolvency proceeding.

events.title: BitMax launched in July 2018
events.description: The centralized exchange later known as AscendEX launched under the BitMax name in July 2018.
events.notes: The reviewed sources establish July 2018 but not an exact public launch day, so the first day of the month is used as a month-level marker.

events.title: AscendEX hot wallets were breached
events.description: AscendEX identified unauthorized transfers from hot-wallet infrastructure across several networks on December 11, 2021 and temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while rebuilding affected infrastructure.
events.notes: The incident caused a temporary service restriction but did not establish a terminal shutdown; the exchange later resumed services.

events.title: AscendEX ceased operations
events.description: AscendEX stated that it ceased operations effective July 1, 2026. New account opening, deposits, trading, swaps, staking, lending, referrals, promotions, and other crypto-asset services ended, leaving only limited wind-down and offboarding access subject to platform and legal constraints.
events.notes: The official notice was published on July 6 but states that cessation took effect on July 1. Automated withdrawals were paused from July 6 and all withdrawal requests moved to manual review. The event confirms operational cessation, but the notice does not establish one exclusive death reason.

evidence.notes: Independent reporting corroborates the July 1 cessation, the cited regulatory, financial, and operational factors, and uncertainty surrounding user withdrawals.
